title: Product Size Reference Photo to Show Scale | AIVideosUGC
description: Make a product size reference photo that sets your item beside a suitcase, phone, or hand. Upload your product photo and show its scale at a glance. Start now.
h1: Product Size Reference Photo Next to Objects Shoppers Know
lead: A product size reference photo starts with a clear picture of your item and pairs it with a familiar object, giving shoppers a visual sense of scale before they read exact measurements.
intro: In the example, a black packable backpack and a matching zip pouch sit on an airport floor beside a silver carry-on, with a traveler reaching for the top handle. Without reading a single number, you can tell the backpack is smaller than the case and the pouch fits in one hand.

Size is one of the first things shoppers wonder about with bags, wallets, watches, jewelry, and fitness gear. A reference photo gives them a feel for scale, while the measurements in your listing give the exact numbers. If you want to show two of your own sizes together, a [Side-by-Side Video template](page:tpl-compare) can put them in one clip before this still photo. Use it as an extra gallery image on Amazon, right after the main photo.
tip: Name the comparison object in your description, such as "next to a carry-on suitcase" or "held in an adult hand," and choose one your buyers already own.

steps.t: Upload the item you will measure
steps.d: Photograph the whole product, including handles, closures, and attached parts.
Place it beside a common object or show it in a person’s hand.
Type the measurements and units in your product listing.

ideas.d: Show a pendant or a pair of studs next to a coin or on a fingertip so shoppers can judge how small they really are.
Set a tote, crossbody, or backpack next to a carry-on or a laptop to show how big it is compared with things people travel with.
Place a keychain, card holder, or lip balm in an open palm for a gift shop listing.

faq.q: Is the size in the photo exact?
faq.a: No. The photo is a visual guide, and the scale between objects can be slightly off. Always write the real measurements in your product description so buyers have the exact numbers.

faq.q: Can I use this as an Amazon listing image?
faq.a: Yes, as one of the extra images in your gallery. A scale shot placed right after the main image helps buyers picture the size before they scroll to the details.

faq.q: What object should I use to show a product’s size?
faq.a: Choose a familiar object with a stable size, such as a standard card or common bottle. Generated scale may vary, so include exact measurements in your product description.

overview.h2: Give Shoppers a Familiar Sense of Scale
overview.p: Dimensions are precise, but shoppers still want to picture a bag in a hand, a pendant at the collarbone, or a case beside the phone it protects. A scale image adds that visual cue to the gallery while leaving the official numbers in your product description.

overview.h2: Choose Context That Matches the Purchase
overview.p: A carry-on helps with travel gear; a palm helps with a keychain. The comparison should be recognizable to the people buying the item and simple enough that the product remains the subject of the frame.

items.d: Use a clean source photo so the chosen reference is added intentionally instead of being confused with your background.
A bank card, phone, coffee mug, adult hand, or carry-on gives more useful context than an object with many sizes.
Ask for a level view and keep the product near the reference so distance does not make one appear artificially large.
Show the full outline, handles, straps, or clasp instead of using a crop that hides the very dimension shoppers need.

results.h2: What a Scale Frame Can Tell

items.d: Show whether a pouch fits in one hand or a tote sits beside a laptop.
Place jewelry or a watch where it is worn so buyers can judge visual presence.
Set a case, bottle, or backpack beside luggage or a seat-side object people already know.
A teardrop necklace resting on an open palm beside a simple coin for a quick size cue.
The bag at a person's side with a paperback or phone visible inside the opening.
A compact charger or speaker next to a laptop corner and a coffee mug on this desk.
A toiletry pouch beside a carry-on handle with one folded shirt nearby to suggest packing scale.

after_download.h2: Pair the Picture With the Numbers

items.d: Compare the visual scene with the real item; discard any frame that makes it look materially larger or smaller.
Write width, height, depth, weight, or chain length in the product page yourself.
Use the scale image as a supporting gallery frame after shoppers have seen the product alone.

fit.h2: Good Matches for a Size Reference
good: Bags, wallets, jewelry, watches, and small accessories
Desk or kitchen products with a familiar everyday comparison
Listings that already publish exact dimensions
not_ideal: Products whose size changes dramatically with perspective or pose
Items that must be measured to a regulated tolerance
A reference object with no stable, recognizable size
